relevant_finding_from_abstract: Future directions listed in abstract: better data collection, organizational factors, ethical implementation, standardized handling of data imbalance, transfer learning across facilities

study: Oikonomidi, Norman, McGarrigle, Stokes, van der Veer, Dowding
data_and_method: Rapid systematic review of RCTs/non-RCTs of interventions that use a no-show predictive model
relevant_finding_from_abstract: Predictive modeling plus text message reminders, phone call reminders, and patient navigator calls are probably effective at reducing no-shows; effect of model-based overbooking uncertain; limited reporting on cost-effectiveness, acceptability, equity
limitation_or_open_point: Our study does not test interventions; it evaluates the prioritization step only
role_in_paper: Introduction + Discussion: why targeting a limited outreach capacity matters; equity/limits
todo_read_sections: Results on risk ratios; equity section

data_and_method: Systematic literature review of no-shows in appointment scheduling (105 of 727 retrieved articles analysed)
relevant_finding_from_abstract: Most commonly reported determinants: high lead time and prior no-show history; younger adults and lower socioeconomic status more likely to no-show; average no-show rate of the order of 23%
role_in_paper: Introduction + feature rationale (lead time) + ethics (socioeconomic proxies)

data_and_method: Systematic literature review of patient no-show prediction
relevant_finding_from_abstract: Reviews state of the art in no-show prediction used to support scheduling systems

study: Ding, Gellad, Mather, Barth, Poon, Newman, Goldstein
data_and_method: Regularized logistic regression on 2,264,235 outpatient appointments (14 specialties, 55 clinics)
validation: Discrimination and calibration at health-system, specialty and clinic level
relevant_finding_from_abstract: Average C-statistic 0.83 across clinic-level models with strong calibration
limitation_or_open_point: EHR from one health system; not the Brazilian public dataset
role_in_paper: Related work: calibration reported in no-show risk models
verification_status: Verified (PMC full record read in search snippet)

data_and_method: Probabilistic classifiers for no-show prediction feeding an appointment-scheduling algorithm
validation: Computational experiments validated on large real-world appointment data
relevant_finding_from_abstract: Selecting classifiers by AUC yields lower schedule efficiency than Log Loss or Brier score; using Log Loss/Brier instead can improve schedule quality by 3-7%
role_in_paper: Introduction + Methods: justification to report Brier/Log Loss, not only AUC/PR-AUC

data_and_method: Two Brazilian datasets: CT appointments (8,371 rows, 6.65% no-show) and Kaggle Espirito Santo subset (7,413 rows after preprocessing, 19.03%); symbolic regression + Instance Hardness Threshold vs KNN/SVM and resampling
relevant_finding_from_abstract: SR + IHT outperformed other algorithms/resampling; sensitivity around 0.95 (dataset 1) and 0.94 (dataset 2); highlights risk of relying on few validation runs
limitation_or_open_point: Uses a Kaggle subset with resampling; evaluation emphasis is sensitivity under resampled/balanced training
role_in_paper: Related work on the Kaggle dataset; contrast: we avoid resampling to preserve probability meaning
todo_read_sections: Evaluation protocol; whether temporal split was used

study: Salazar, Leithardt, Parreira, da Rocha Fernandes, Barbosa, Correia
data_and_method: ML no-show prediction on a private dataset (~5,000 samples) from a Brazilian university health center; compares with the public Kaggle dataset context
relevant_finding_from_abstract: States that the Kaggle dataset (public hospitals in Vitoria, Espirito Santo) is the only publicly available no-show dataset most researchers have used; Random Forest performed best on their data

data_and_method: ML no-show prediction combined with scheduling optimisation; real clinic and simulated data
relevant_finding_from_abstract: If a racial group has higher no-show risk, ML-driven overbooking schedules that group into overbooked slots disproportionately, causing longer waits
limitation_or_open_point: US specialty clinic; race attribute not present in the Kaggle dataset
role_in_paper: Discussion/ethics: risk of proxy attributes (e.g., neighbourhood, scholarship)
